name: Jasion RetroVolt Electric Bike
verdict: The best all-around e-bike — full suspension, fat tires, and up to 70 miles of range in a retro-styled ride.
description: The RetroVolt is our favorite all-rounder because it's comfortable almost anywhere. Full suspension and fat tires soak up potholes, gravel, and sand, so it works for commuting during the week and the beach or trail on weekends. A removable 48V 15Ah battery is rated for up to 70 miles, and a motor rated at 2000W peak gives you strong acceleration up hills. Five riding modes, a 7-speed drivetrain, and an IPX6 water-resistance rating round it out.
cons: Top speed exceeds Class 2 limits in many areas — check local rules

name: Heybike Ranger 2.0 Folding E-Bike
verdict: The best folding e-bike — a fat-tire, step-thru frame that folds for the car trunk or apartment, with a 600Wh battery.
description: The Ranger 2.0 solves the biggest e-bike problem: where to put it. The frame folds, so it fits in a car trunk, a closet, or a small apartment, and the step-thru design makes it easy to get on and off. Don't let the folding frame fool you, though. Its 20-inch fat tires handle rough pavement and dirt, the motor is rated at 2000W peak, and the removable 600Wh battery is rated for up to 70 miles.
cons: Top speed exceeds Class 2 limits in many areas — check local rules
Smaller wheels feel twitchier at speed

name: Gotrax R1 Folding E-Bike
verdict: The best lightweight and budget e-bike — just 45 pounds, folds up, and has a gentle 350W motor for easy commutes.
description: The Gotrax R1 is the e-bike for people who don't want a heavy machine. At about 45 pounds it's light for an e-bike, and the folding frame makes it easy to carry up stairs or toss in a trunk. The 350W motor tops out at 20 mph, which keeps it within common e-bike rules and makes it approachable for new riders. A 48V battery is rated for up to 40 miles on the lowest pedal-assist level, and an LCD display shows your speed and five assist levels.
cons: Rated range is at the lowest assist level

name: Jasion EB5 MAX Fat-Tire E-Bike
verdict: A powerful fat-tire mountain e-bike with commuter extras — cruise control, fenders, and a rear rack included.
description: The EB5 MAX takes Jasion's popular EB5 and adds muscle and practicality. The motor is rated at 2000W peak, the 48V 15Ah (720Wh) battery gives you plenty of range, and 26×4-inch fat tires grip loose ground. What makes it great for daily riding are the extras that usually cost more: cruise control for long flat stretches, fenders to keep you clean, and a rear rack for bags or groceries.
cons: Top speed exceeds Class 2 limits in many areas — check local rules

name: Jasion EB5 Electric Mountain Bike
verdict: A great-value commuter and trail e-bike — a 26-inch mountain frame, front suspension, and a 7-speed drivetrain.
description: The original EB5 is one of the most popular entry-level e-bikes for good reason. Its 26-inch mountain-bike frame and front suspension fork handle bike paths and light trails comfortably, and the 7-speed drivetrain lets you pedal efficiently when you want the exercise. The motor is rated at 1000W peak, and the removable battery is rated for up to 40 miles, which covers most commutes with charge to spare.
pros: Works on paths and light trails
cons: Shorter rated range than bigger-battery models
